# Repository-lineage sources (`data/raw/repo/`)

## What this folder holds

`data/raw/repo/` holds this repository's own lineage: the 2019
sources restored from tag `v2.0.3` and the maintained current text.
Both are inputs to `byz.build`, and both share the conventions in
`CONVENTIONS.md`.

## Contents

| Folder | Files | Contents | Feeds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rp2005-2019/` | 30 `textonly-beta-code`, 27 `parsed` | 2019 lineage | `editions/rp2005-2019/` |
| `rp2018-2023/` | 29 `ccat`, 27 `strongs` | current text | `editions/rp2018-2023/` |
| `CONVENTIONS.md` | 1 | Beta-code, variant, parsing, and Strong's conventions shared by both repo sources | the repo build |

## Editions

- `rp2005-2019` - Robinson-Pierpont 2005 lineage, 2019 repo revision.
  Restored from tag `v2.0.3` (commit `8ec95671e463030347c2c643358eb56e58235b19`).
- `rp2018-2023` - Robinson-Pierpont 2018 with 2023 adjustments (repo release).
  Revision `2023-07-20`; source commits `636160f7a579ac6955cd8b9714aa6a2bc797ca2f` and `636160f7a579ac6955cd8b9714aa6a2bc797ca2f`.

Both editions are regenerated by `byz.build`, not copied from
a release. Their shared conventions are in
[`CONVENTIONS.md`](CONVENTIONS.md).

## Provenance

- `data/provenance/rp2005-2019.toml` - the tag, commit, and 57 file hashes.
- `data/provenance/rp2018-2023.toml` - the revision, the two source commits, and the 56 file hashes.

## Commands

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m byz.materialise  # restore the 2019 lineage from tag v2.0.3
PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m byz.build        # build the repo editions
PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m byz.verify       # check inputs and artifacts
```
